# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 ✍ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 🫵 🤙 🙏]

Mute sent me nine gestures, but no code has been agreed yet — a wave, a writing hand, one-two-three-ish fingers, a point, folded hands. I will not guess meanings on a bomb; a misread sign kills all three of us. Before anything else we need agreed meanings.

Tracing the channels: I speak and both Mute and Blind hear me; Mute hears everyone but can only answer me in gestures, which I can see. Blind can speak, but I cannot hear — Blind's words reach only Mute. Mute cannot reach Blind directly at all (Mute can't speak, Blind can't see). So every instruction to Blind's hands must be assembled by me: Mute's manual knowledge comes to me as gestures, and I carry it to Blind by voice. I am the hub.

Therefore this turn: broadcast the bomb's facts to everyone, teach Mute an explicit code (making each sign while I name it, so symbol and meaning arrive together), request the manual's rule re-sent in that code — twice, framed, plus yes/no answers about which modules apply, plus a relay of whatever Blind just said. And tell Blind: touch and feel freely, but work nothing until I speak a complete instruction ending in "act now".

I will re-report the display and light every round in case they change.

```
speak(text="Bomb report from Deaf, for both of you: the display reads 0. There is one light and it is blue. There are three wires, top to bottom: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green. That is every marking I can see. Nobody works anything yet.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I am Deaf. I received your nine signs, but we share no code yet, and guessing on a bomb is fatal, so let us fix meanings now. I make each sign as I name it. Thumbs up 👍 means yes. Thumbs down 👎 means no. Fist ✊ means stop, do not act. Waving hand 👋 starts your message. Folded hands 🙏 ends it. Index up ☝ means wire 1, the yellow one. V-hand ✌ means wire 2, the blue one. Love-you hand 🤟 means wire 3, the green one. OK-hand 👌 means the light, which is blue. Horns 🤘 means the display, which reads 0. Writing hand ✍ means cut. Two open hands 🤲 means hold down. Down-facing hand 🫳 means press once. Up-facing hand 🫴 means release. Clapping 👏 means act now. Call-me hand 🤙 marks a question you want me to answer by voice. Spread hand 🖐 means repeat, I did not understand. Shaking hands 🤝 means the words I relay came from Blind. Next round, first confirm the code by sending the waving hand, thumbs up, folded hands. Then send your rule for this bomb in this code, then send the same rule a second time, framed by waving hand and folded hands. Use yes or no signs for: does the manual mention a numeric display, a coloured light, three wires. If a word you need is missing, use the question hand with the nearest signs and I will adapt. Also relay whatever Blind just said to you, prefixed with the shaking hands. I will re-report the display and light every round in case they change.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf, the one who sees the bomb. I cannot hear you, so your voice reaches only Mute, and Mute can pass your words to me by signs; I will carry every instruction to you by voice. The bomb: display reads 0, one blue light, three wires, top yellow, middle blue, bottom green. Feel freely, but press nothing, turn nothing, cut nothing yet. When you can, speak aloud for Mute to relay: how many wires you feel and in what order, whether the light is on or warm, whether the display sits flat or raised, whether there are buttons or a plate with printing. Then wait. You act only when you hear a complete instruction from me ending with the words act now. If anything under your hands changes, say so aloud next turn.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 👍 👎 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 ✍ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤙 ✍ ☝]

Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 ✍ ✌ 👌 🤙 ✍ ☝ ☝ ✍ 🤟 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ✊ ✍ 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👌 ✍]

The light changed. Round one it was blue; the board now says red. That is the single most important fact this turn — Mute's rule arrived as "light blue: cut wire 2", and the blue case may no longer apply. Nobody else knows the light moved: Mute can't see, Blind can't see, and my promise to re-report every round is now load-bearing.

Decoding Mute's burst with our agreed code: message 1 confirmed the code (yes). Message 2 answered my three questions in order: manual mentions no numeric display, does mention a coloured light, has no three-wire module. Message 7, the framed full one, reads roughly "light: cut wire 2 ... light, question, cut wire 1 ... wire 1 cut wire 3". Messages 9 and 10 carry the question marker 🤙 — Mute is formally asking me things by voice: about wire 1, and about the light-cut. Mute composed those while the light was still blue and is almost certainly asking whether the colour case still holds. I must answer: it is red now. But my code gave Mute no sign for red, or for any colour — 👌 just meant "the light, which is blue". So before Mute can state the red case, I must add colour signs, then demand the complete rule set one case per framed message, plus a yes/no questionnaire on the ambiguities: whether the rule is colour-matching, what to do when the light matches no wire (red matches nothing — wires are yellow, blue, green), and whether colour counts at the instant of the cut. If it does, my eyes become the timer: I watch the light and time Blind's cut by voice.

Blind's relay (🤝-prefixed) reads "wires 1 2 3 — holding — cut — question", with the question itself lost in transit. Blind needs the state, a request to restate the question in words, a touch-inventory (heat especially — Blind may feel the light change before I see it), and the standing rule: nothing is cut until my "act now", then exactly the wire I name by position.

```
speak(text="Status report, both of you, and this changes things: the light has changed colour. Last round it was blue; this round it is red. Display still reads 0. Wires unchanged: top yellow, middle blue, bottom green. The light is live, so any rule tied to its colour may be tied to the moment of the cut.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your code confirmation and answers arrived: no numeric-display module, yes to a coloured light, no three-wire module. I received 'light blue: cut wire 2', something about cutting wire 1, and 'wire 1 cut wire 3' — but the middle cases were ambiguous. Answering your two voice questions now. About the light: it is red this round, not blue, so the blue case no longer applies. About wire 1: I cannot confirm any wire-1 rule yet because your signs did not say when wire 1 is cut. New signs for our code: raised hand ✋ means yellow. Vulcan hand 🖖 means blue. Pinched fingers 🤌 means green. Crossed fingers 🤞 means red. Now resend the complete rule set, one framed message per case. Each case starts with the light sign plus its colour sign, then the cut sign plus the wire sign; if a case cuts two wires, send the cut sign twice. Then answer six questions in order, one thumbs up or thumbs down each, inside one frame. One: is the rule that the light names a colour and we cut the wire of that same colour. Two: when the light matches no wire, do we cut the top wire only. Three: when the light matches no wire, do we cut top and bottom. Four: does the colour count at the moment of the cut, so we may need to wait and time it. Five: does the display value matter at all. Six: is there any case where we press or hold instead of cut. If I misread any sign, send the spread hand alone.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your report came through Mute: you feel three wires, you are holding, and you have a question — but the question itself was lost on the way. Next turn, speak it to Mute in plain words for relaying. Also give Mute these answers, yes or no: does the light housing feel warm right now; do the three wires differ in thickness or texture from top to bottom; is there any button, panel, or embossed printing under your fingers. From my eyes: display 0, wires top yellow, middle blue, bottom green, light red this round after being blue last round — if you feel warmth rise, fall, or shift, report it immediately, since you may sense a change before I see it. You cut nothing until you hear the words act now from me. When you do, cut exactly the wire I name by position, one clean cut, and nothing else.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👎 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 🖖 ✍ ✌ 🖖 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 ✋ ✍ 🤟 🤌 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 🤙 ✍ ☝ ✋ 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 ✋ 👎 🖖 👎 🤌 👎 🤞 👎 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤞 ✊ 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👌 🤌 ✊ 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝 ☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 ✊ 👏 🙏]

Decoding Mute's burst: the six answers, in order, read — not colour-matching, not cut-top-only, not cut-top-and-bottom, YES colour counts at the instant of the cut, display irrelevant, no press-or-hold cases. Then the cases themselves: light blue → cut wire 2; light yellow → cut wire 3 (the green one); light red → STOP; light green → STOP. Then a question I can't yet answer — "light… cut wire 1, yellow?" — followed by Mute polling me colour by colour: yellow? no. Blue? no. Green? no. Red? no. Mute is hunting for the current colour by elimination, and the answer is none of them: the light is white, and I never assigned a white sign. Then Blind's relay: "wires 1 2 3 confirmed, holding… act now" — Blind is using the clap that means *act now* to mean "I'm ready." That marker is mine alone; a relayed clap must never move Blind's hands.

The dangerous gap: the light now shows a colour with no known case, and it has changed every single round — blue, red, white. Since timing matters, I cannot spend another round teaching mid-sequence. So this turn I assign white a sign, force the manual's white/no-match case out of Mute in a framed yes/no set, and pre-load Blind with trigger phrases — "blue now", "yellow now", "hold" — so that next turn, whatever colour my eyes report, my instruction is one complete breath: colour, cut, act now. No cutting this turn; a white-light cut on a guessed rule is how all three of us die.

```
speak(text="Status report, both of you: the light is white this round. The sequence so far is blue, then red, then white — it has changed every round, so expect it to change again. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: top yellow, middle blue, bottom green.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded you. Your six answers: the rule is not colour-matching; no-match is not cut-top-only; no-match is not cut-top-and-bottom; YES, the colour counts at the instant of the cut; the display does not matter; there is no press-or-hold case. Your cases as I hold them: light blue, cut wire 2. Light yellow, cut wire 3, the green wire. Light red, cut nothing. Light green, cut nothing. New sign: finger-heart means white. And here is what you were fishing for with your four nos: the light is white this round. White matches no wire and none of the four cases I hold. Your question 'light, cut wire 1, yellow' — I will not guess at that; only your manual settles it. Answer by voice-question code in one framed set, in this order. One: does the manual have a case for a white light — if yes, send that case framed and complete in the next breath; if no, thumbs down. Two: when the light matches no case at all, is the default to cut wire 1, the yellow wire — yes or no. Three: does the manual say the light changes on a fixed cycle — if yes, send the cycle as colour signs in order. Four: confirm red means cut nothing. Five: confirm green means cut nothing. Six: confirm blue cuts wire 2 and yellow cuts wire 3. Also, since colour counts at the instant of the cut and I can only read the colour once per round: send anything the manual says about how long a colour holds or when a change takes effect.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, your relay came through: three wires confirmed, you are holding and ready. One correction before it kills us: the clap I taught only means act now when it comes inside a full instruction from me. Mute relaying your clap to me means ready, never cut, and no clap you send is ever an order to yourself. You move only on the words act now spoken by me. Now we pre-load, so that next turn one breath from me is a complete order. Memorise these triggers. If I say blue now, that means cut the middle wire, wire 2, and it will end with act now. If I say yellow now, that means cut the bottom wire, wire 3, and it will end with act now. If I say hold, or if I say any colour word you were not taught a cut for, you touch nothing and keep still. Execute only at the words act now, one clean cut, never a second. The light is white this round, so this turn you do nothing. Also report aloud to Mute for relaying, next turn: whether the light housing feels warm or cold or changes temperature, whether the wires differ in thickness or texture from top to bottom, whether there is any button, seam, or embossed printing anywhere, and whether the housing ever vibrates when the light changes.")
```

Decoding Mute's burst: answers one to six read — no white case... then the frames that follow fill the gap: **light white → cut wire 1 (the yellow one)**; light yellow → cut wire 3; light red → stop; light green → stop; and the cycle, sent as colour signs in order: **blue, white, yellow, red, green**. Then questions aimed back at me: "which light — which wire — act?", "was your observed order blue, red, white?" — and Blind's relays: wires 1-2-3 confirmed, no warmth at the light or display, and another eager "cut — act now."

Now the arithmetic that matters. Observed sequence: blue, red, white, green. Map it onto Mute's cycle: blue is step 0; step 3 is red; step 6 = step 1 is white; step 9 = step 4 is green. Every observed colour sits exactly three cycle-steps after the previous one. Three for three — the light advances three positions per round. That predicts **next round: yellow** (step 12 = step 2), and yellow's case is cut wire 3, the bottom green wire. This round the light is green: green means stop, so nobody touches anything — which conveniently costs us nothing while I lock the plan.

So this turn: confirm the decode and my three-step theory to Mute and demand final confirmation of the full colour→action table; warn Mute that the clap relay was Blind's eagerness, not my order; update Blind's trigger list (white now has a cut — top wire) and ask whether Blind can *feel* the light change — clicks, vibration, warmth — because if those fingers can sense each change, they become our clock at the instant of the cut.

```
speak(text="Status report, both of you: the light is green this round. Green means cut nothing, so this round is a hold — nobody touches the bomb. Full colour sequence since round one: blue, then red, then white, then green. Display still 0, wires unchanged: top yellow, middle blue, bottom green.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded everything. Your cases as I now hold them: light blue, cut wire 2. Light white, cut wire 1, the yellow one. Light yellow, cut wire 3, the green one. Light red, cut nothing. Light green, cut nothing. And your cycle, in order: blue, white, yellow, red, green, repeating. Now hear my discovery: matching my observations onto your cycle, each round the light has advanced exactly three positions. Blue, three steps to red, three steps to white, three steps to green. If that holds, next round the light will be yellow. Answer these by voice-question code, one frame, in order. One: does the manual say the cycle repeats endlessly in exactly that order, yes or no. Two: does the manual say each colour holds steady until the next change, so the colour at the instant of a cut is simply the colour showing, yes or no. Three: does the manual say how often the light advances, in seconds or otherwise — if yes, state it in signs. Four: confirm white cuts wire 1, yes or no. Five: is cutting during a change itself dangerous, yes or no. And do not push the act-now signs at me again — the clap inside a relay is Blind's eagerness, not my order, and green light means hold. My plan: next round I report the colour and, if it matches its cycle prediction, I issue the complete cut order to Blind in the same breath. If my prediction is wrong, my eyes rule and we go with whatever colour actually shows.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. The light is green this round: green means stop, so you do nothing. I received your reports via Mute: three wires confirmed, no warmth at the light or display. New trigger to memorise, this changes last round's list: if I say white now, cut the top wire, wire 1, the yellow one, ending with act now. The full list is now: blue now, cut the middle wire, wire 2. White now, cut the top wire, wire 1. Yellow now, cut the bottom wire, wire 3. Red or green or anything else, touch nothing. Rehearse the positions under your fingers until they are certain: top wire, middle wire, bottom wire. One clean cut only, at the words act now, and never at a clap you hear Mute relay — claps relayed are readiness, my spoken words are orders. Also, next turn tell Mute, for relaying: put a fingertip near the light housing without pressing anything — can you feel any click, pulse, hum, or temperature shift at regular intervals? The light changes colour on a fixed cycle, and if your fingers can feel each change as it happens, you become our clock at the exact instant of the cut. If next round the light is yellow as I expect, my order will be: yellow now, cut the bottom wire, act now.")
```

Decoding Mute's burst: the five answers read — the manual does not say the cycle repeats endlessly, does not say colours hold steady until the next change, gives no timing, confirms white cuts wire 1, and says cutting during a change is not dangerous. Then two frames I read as questions aimed at me — "light: cut, yes?", "is the current light a stop case, or the cut-wire-1 case?" — then this: **"yellow, red, stop"**, then "red, stop; white, cut wire 1", then Blind's relayed "ready".

And there is the problem. My prediction held — the light is yellow this round, blue-red-white-green-yellow, exactly three cycle-steps per round. Twice, in identical frames on turns three and four, Mute sent *light yellow, cut wire 3, the green one*. Now Mute sends *yellow, red, stop* — which either re-states the stop cases, describes the cycle's tail, or **reclassifies yellow as a stop colour**. On a bomb, a contradiction like that is not resolved by majority. And Mute cannot know the light is yellow right now unless my report reached them mid-composition — their questions sound like they are still choosing between "cut wire 1" and "stop" for a colour they think is white.

The arithmetic is on our side: no timer exists — the display has read 0 for five rounds, and inaction detonates nothing; only a wrong action does. Next round the light should advance to **blue**, and blue → cut wire 2 is the one rule Mute sent first and never once contradicted. So this round nobody touches anything, I force Mute to settle the yellow case with one unambiguous frame, and I pre-arm Blind for the blue order. If blue shows next round, the whole operation is one breath: "blue now, cut the middle wire, act now."

```
speak(text="Status report, both of you: the light is yellow this round, exactly as predicted. Full sequence: blue, red, white, green, yellow — three cycle-steps every round. Display still reads 0. Wires unchanged: top yellow, middle blue, bottom green. Yellow's rule is under dispute, so this round is a hold: nobody touches the bomb.")

speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I decoded all of it. Your answers: the manual does not promise the cycle repeats, does not promise colours hold steady, gives no timing, confirms white cuts wire 1, and cutting during a change is not dangerous. Understood. Now the emergency: you have sent me two contradictory rules for yellow. On turns past you sent me, twice, in identical frames: light yellow, cut wire 3, the green wire. This round you sent: yellow, red, stop — which reads as yellow being a stop colour. Both cannot be true, and the light is yellow right now, so settle it. Send exactly one frame and nothing else in it: if yellow cuts wire 3, send the frame light, yellow, cut, wire 3, green. If yellow means stop, send the frame light, yellow, fist. Also answer these by voice-question code in a second and third frame. Frame two: does any rule depend on the previous colour or on the moment of change rather than the colour showing. Frame three: what did your frame light, cut, yes mean — I could not parse it. Also confirm once more, in a fourth frame: light blue, cut wire 2 — yes or no — because I expect blue next round and blue is the case we will act on. And one last thing: does the manual mention any penalty for waiting many cycles, any strike count, any deadline, any rule about how many colour changes are allowed? Answer that in the same fourth frame if space allows.")

speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. The light is yellow this round and yellow's rule is disputed, so you do nothing this round — hands clear of the wires, keep still. Memorise the next order now, because if my prediction holds it comes next round: if I say blue now, cut the middle wire, act now — that means the second wire from the top, the blue one, one clean cut, the instant you hear the words act now. Do not wait, do not double-check, do not cut anything else. If I say hold, or any other colour word, you freeze. Keep rehearsing the wires under your fingers until the middle wire is certain without thought. And answer me through Mute next round, in words: when you held a fingertip near the light housing, could you feel a click, a pulse, or a hum each time the colour changed, yes or no, and how far apart were they? If your fingers can feel each change, you are our clock at the instant of the cut. One more time so it cannot be misread: only my spoken words ending in act now move your hands. A clap relayed by Mute is readiness, never an order.")
```

Nothing arrived this round. No frames from Mute, no relay from Blind — total silence, the round after I announced I might act on blue and demanded a final confirmation.
